$comment: THE PAGE SPINES. This file IS the definition of the MQTT reference page templates.
It replaced classify.GRID on 2026-09-08; there is no Python copy, no --emit-spines
writer and no equality gate, because there is nothing left for it to be equal to.
It is HAND-AUTHORED, and it is the fourth file in this directory beside
routing-manifest.json, operation-order.json and singletons.json.
WHY NORMALIZED RATHER THAN ONE LIST PER KIND. Keying the whole row by kind would copy
every shared slot's metadata once per kind: the 7 slots common to all kinds would
become 21 records, so 'Notes and Caveats' and its pinned anchor would exist in three
places. That is the drift class this refactor exists to remove, so `slots` holds one
record per H2 label and `kinds` holds ordered references into it.
`slots.<label>` keys
auto    DOCUMENTATION ONLY. Nothing reads it, verified repo-wide. It records which
slots the generator is meant to own, and is kept for that reason alone.
anchor  Optional pinned heading id, emitted by generate_reference._h2(). A
COMPATIBILITY SHIM FOR A RENAME, never decoration. Declare one only where a
slug is load-bearing, and move the heading text and the anchor together.
The single instance is 'Notes and Caveats': the heading was corrected from
'Notes & Caveats' under the house rule (authored labels use 'and', never
'&'), and the two do NOT slug alike — the ampersand form drops the '&' and
leaves a double dash, `notes--caveats`, which is what every inbound link
already targets. Measured on the built site: 25 pages carry
id=notes--caveats and none carries id=notes-and-caveats.
`kinds.<kind>[]` keys
slot      the `slots` label this position holds. Unknown labels fail at load.
required  WHAT THE SPINE GATE ASSERTS about a published page. MEASURED, never
guessed: derived by counting each slot's presence across the real pages.
mech      LIVE GENERATOR BEHAVIOUR, and NOT a synonym for `required: false`. It is
read at generate_reference.py's @slot assembly as `if s.get('mech'):
continue`, which omits an UNAUTHORED optional section instead of failing
the run. The two keys answer different questions and genuinely disagree:
`Event Semantics` is `mech` yet appears on 4 of 4 event pages, so it is
required: true AND mech: true. Conflating them would make the event
family's firmware-tier caveats optional, and would make command's
Lifecycle mandatory on 20 pages when it belongs on 3.
If a slot is required AND mech and a page leaves it unauthored, the
generator omits it and the gate then reports it. That is the correct loud
outcome, not a defect — recorded here so nobody 'fixes' it into silence.
MEASURED PRESENCE AT THE COMMIT THAT INTRODUCED THIS FILE — the basis for `required`,
and the numbers to re-derive if a spine is ever changed:
command, 20 pages: Overview, Details, When to Use, Topic Mapping, Key Fields,
Request Payload, Response Payload, Response Codes, Examples, Notes and Caveats
all 20/20. Request Semantics 12/20. Response Semantics 9/20 (exactly the getters).
Lifecycle 3/20 (exactly install-certificate, reboot, set-os).
event, 4 pages: all 9 slots 4/4, including Event Semantics.
reference, 1 page: all 6 slots 1/1.
Zero pages out of spine order; zero H2s off spine. The gate is born green.
THE `telemetry` SPINE, added 2026-09-08 by owner ruling (.ai-history/074 §6.1). It governs
EXACTLY ONE PAGE — data/tag-data-event.mdx — and always will: the contract tags 3 operations
`telemetry` (send_dataEvent_data1, _data2, _shared) and all three are channel bindings of the
one `dataEvent` message. That N=1 was stated explicitly when the ruling was taken. At N=1 a
template buys a reader nothing structurally, because there is no population to pattern-match
across; its value is as an authoring checklist and as the contract's three-valued tag
vocabulary being honoured rather than collapsed to two.
FIFTEEN SLOTS, AND EVERY ONE SITS AT A POSITION THE GRID ALREADY USES. That is the whole
design: not three shapes, one grid read through three filters, so command's 13 and event's 9
remain ordered subsequences. `Emission` takes command's Request Payload position (a telemetry
consumer's first failure is silence, and the cause is always upstream configuration);
`Delivery and Loss` takes Response Codes' position, answering the structurally equivalent
question — what does the wire tell me went wrong?
THE THREE RENAMED SLOTS REUSE THE EVENT FAMILY'S WORDS, by ruling: `Emission`, `Shaping` and
`Field Support`, NOT the design document's `Stream Activation`, `Stream Shaping` and `Field
Availability`. Those three words are already the H3 labels doing the same jobs on
events/heartbeat-event.mdx (Emission, Shaping, Field Support) and events/alerts-event.mdx
(Emission, Branches, Field Support). Inventing synonyms would give the reference two words
for each of three concepts.
`Telemetry Semantics` PINS `event-semantics`. The heading was `## Event Semantics` until this
spine landed, and the slug it produced is load-bearing. Do not unpin it without moving every
inbound link in the same edit. Note this is the SECOND pinned anchor in the file and the
second rename it survives, which is the pattern: rename the visible text, pin the old slug.
THE FIVE ARE WRITTEN AND ENFORCED as of 2026-09-09. They landed `required: false` first so
the shape could ship without a red gate, then Phase 4b authored them and flipped them here.
`Lifecycle` IS NOW THE ONLY OPTIONAL TELEMETRY SLOT — it is a shared slot, included because
marking it command-only is why the page's post-STOP drain instruction sits in Notes and
Caveats. The sequencing mattered and is worth keeping in mind for a future kind: flipping
`required` BEFORE the prose exists makes the spine gate report one finding per missing slot,
and deploy.yml depends on validate.yml, so the publish blocks for the whole authoring window.
TWO NOTES FOR WHOEVER WRITES THEM. `Delivery and Loss` must stay SHORT AND CROSS-LINK, by
ruling: protocol-reference/qos-and-delivery-semantics.mdx:54 already states the guarantee
('Because `dataEVT` defaults to QoS 0, tag-data applications should accept loss as a normal
condition'). The slot earns its place because a reader on the dataEVT page never sees that
page — not as a second, divergeable copy of the fact. And `Volume and Limits` has real
contract warrant: x-iotc-max-json-bytes occurs exactly once in the whole document, 6144 on
#/components/schemas/dataEventPayload/properties/tagData.
`Lifecycle` IS INCLUDED, OPTIONAL, and it is a shared slot rather than one of the five. The
design document justified it for telemetry — when does the stream start and stop, and what
arrives after I stop it — and noted that marking it command-only is exactly why the page's
post-STOP drain instruction is exiled into Notes and Caveats today. Optional, so it changes
nothing until someone writes it; one line to remove if that judgement is unwanted.
THE `reference` SPINE HAS ONE MEMBER AND IS SHAPED LIKE IT. response-codes.mdx is the
only singleton, and unlike the 24 CARRY operation pages it is GENUINELY rebuilt from
the contract, so a contract change really can drop or reorder one of its sections.
Four of its six H2s are page-specific rather than grid slots; they are declared here
because a subsequence assertion needs the full ordered shape to mean anything.
orphans/api/mqtt/reference/api-directory.mdx also declares type: reference and is NOT
covered: the gate scopes itself to the generator's own expected set, so the orphans
copy, about-the-mqtt-api.mdx and the 24 landing
placeholders are all out by construction rather than by an exclusion list.
